title: Ash-Shakur, the Appreciative
hook: the Appreciative, rewarding the smallest good
tomorrow: why say 'Most High' with your forehead on the floor?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Ghafur, who covers faults and forgives them under the cover. The line: he covers. Today, a Name that notices the good instead, down to the smallest drop.

The barista who remembers your order. The neighbor who drags your bin back from the curb. Small things, and the thank-you that would fit them usually never gets said. Yesterday's question: a man, a thirsty dog, a shoe full of water, who says thank you? Here's the hadith. A man on the road, dying of thirst, finds a well, climbs down, and drinks. Back up top, a dog is panting, licking the damp ground. The man thinks: this dog is as thirsty as I was. So he climbs down again, fills his leather shoe with water, holds it in his teeth, climbs back up, and lets the dog drink.
screen: `THE BIN BACK FROM THE CURB.` → `A DOG LICKING DAMP GROUND.` → `A SHOE FULL OF WATER.`

segments.voice: And the hadith says, plainly: Allah thanked him, and forgave him. That's the line to tell a friend tonight. In this story, God is the one who says thank you. That's today's Name. Ash-Shakur, the Appreciative, who rewards the smallest good. Not a big donation, not a famous deed. One shoe of water for one dog, and it's noticed. The companions were surprised too. Is there reward for us even with animals? they asked. In every living being, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said, there is reward. And in another hadith he said: don't look down on any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face. So the smallest good has a witness who appreciates it. And thanks runs the other way too. The Prophet said that whoever doesn't thank people hasn't thanked Allah. Shukr, gratitude, isn't a feeling saved for prayer. It's a note on a locker, a word to the person who stayed late. If Ash-Shakur notices a shoe of water, nothing anyone does for you is too small to notice back.
screen: `ALLAH THANKED HIM.` · `IN EVERY LIVING BEING, REWARD.` · `EVEN A CHEERFUL FACE.` · `THANK PEOPLE, THANK ALLAH.` · then, large: `NOTHING IS TOO SMALL.`

segments.voice: Pour a glass of water, or pick up whatever you're drinking. Take a slow sip and notice it all: how cool it is, its weight on your tongue, the swallow. With each sip through the sit, let one person who made your day a little easier come to mind, and thank them silently by name.
screen: `A GLASS OF WATER.` · `ONE SIP, ONE NAME.`

segments.voice: Ash-Shakur. The Appreciative, who thanked a man for a shoe of water and rewards the smallest good.
Hold on to this: nothing is too small, not the good you do and not the good done for you. Day fifteen-oh-nine is in.

howItsDone: Muslims practice shukr, thanking Allah with words like alhamdulillah and by thanking people; the story of the man who watered a thirsty dog is retold to teach that no good deed is too small.

original.note: Arabic: the Appreciative, the one who thanks and rewards even the smallest good.

trapdoor: what you thought: God is grateful? that sounds backward.
what it means: the Appreciative, who notices and rewards the smallest good, as when He thanked a man for watering a dog.
what a scholar hears: 'fa-shakara Allahu lahu' in Sahih al-Bukhari 2363 and Sahih Muslim 2244; Muslim 2626 on not belittling good; Abu Dawud 4811 on thanking people.
